issues.body: The reverse scan skips `CLASS_IDLE`, so failures on opposite sides of confirmed empty-frontier ticks are counted as one consecutive run. For example, `zero, zero, zero, idle` closes the alert, but the very next `zero` reopens it immediately because all four zero records remain in `zd_tail`; likewise `zero, idle, zero, zero` fires despite only two failing ticks after the frontier was observed empty. `idle` is no longer absence of evidence: this change defines it as positive evidence that no work was ready. Such evidence interrupts the condition "planned ready work but launched nothing" and must break the consecutive failing-tick sequence. Preserving the old recordless semantics after adding this new observation defeats the threshold on re-entry and can cause alert flapping. The added interleaving test pins the unsound behavior rather than detecting it.
issues.fix_hint: Treat `CLASS_IDLE` as a boundary when constructing `zd_tail` (as a productive success already is), while retaining the newest-idle recovery behavior. Add a regression showing that `zero, zero, zero, idle, zero` remains recovered and that three new zero-dispatch ticks after the idle boundary are required to fire again; change the interleaved-idle assertion to verify that the run is reset.
issues.title: An idle observation fails to reset the consecutive zero-dispatch run

verdict.summary: The round-1 finding is fixed: `idle` now requires a successful claim and a raw, mapping-shaped summary carrying type-strict `planned`, `dispatched`, and `defer_reasons` fields, and the added tests cover omitted fields, wrong containers, booleans, and the real summary producer. However, the new classifier treats a positive empty-frontier observation as transparent to the consecutive zero-dispatch run. That contradicts the run's meaning and allows stale pre-idle failures to re-arm the alert after only one or two new failing ticks. Because this is a new major finding relative to round 1, progress is regressing.
